from rest_framework import serializers
from .models import DeveloperProject, WebhookDestination

class WebhookConfigSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    destination_id = serializers.IntegerField()
    events = serializers.ListField(child=serializers.CharField())

class DeveloperProjectSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    webhook = WebhookConfigSerializer(write_only=True, required=False)

    class Meta:
        model = DeveloperProject
        fields = ['project_name', 'webhook']

    def update(self, instance, validated_data):
        webhook_data = validated_data.pop('webhook', None)
        instance.project_name = validated_data.get('project_name', instance.project_name)
        instance.save()

        if webhook_data:
            dest_id = webhook_data['destination_id']
            # Attaches webhook destination to project without checking tenant ownership
            destination = WebhookDestination.objects.get(id=dest_id)
            destination.project = instance
            destination.subscribed_events = webhook_data['events']
            destination.save(update_fields=['project', 'subscribed_events'])
        return instance
diagnosis: DeveloperProjectSerializer allows configuring projects and attaching webhook destinations. When webhook data is supplied, update() fetches WebhookDestination.objects.get(id=dest_id) and attaches it to the project without verifying that the destination belongs to request.user.organization. An attacker can steal another tenant's webhook destination or intercept event streams routed to confidential internal endpoints.

corrected_code:
from rest_framework import serializers
from .models import DeveloperProject, WebhookDestination

class WebhookConfigSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    destination_id = serializers.IntegerField()
    events = serializers.ListField(child=serializers.CharField())

class DeveloperProjectSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    webhook = WebhookConfigSerializer(write_only=True, required=False)

    class Meta:
        model = DeveloperProject
        fields = ['project_name', 'webhook']

    def update(self, instance, validated_data):
        webhook_data = validated_data.pop('webhook', None)
        instance.project_name = validated_data.get('project_name', instance.project_name)
        instance.save()

        if webhook_data:
            dest_id = webhook_data['destination_id']
            # Enforce that the destination belongs to the authenticated user's organization
            user_org = self.context['request'].user.organization
            destination = WebhookDestination.objects.get(id=dest_id, organization=user_org)
            destination.project = instance
            destination.subscribed_events = webhook_data['events']
            destination.save(update_fields=['project', 'subscribed_events'])
        return instance
